page: Amazon Web Services m8idn.large is an x86_64 general-purpose compute instance based on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by dedicated Intel processor hardware operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. It provisions 2 virtual CPUs across a single physical core with multithreading enabled at 2 threads per core, backed by 8.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio.

Hardware integration includes an integrated 118 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume. This embedded local storage provides high-throughput, low-latency disk operations directly attached to the host, bypassing remote storage networking for ephemeral files. For external connectivity, the instance provides a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps alongside native EBS and network optimizations.

The hardware configuration provides balanced resource density for workloads needing modest CPU capability paired with fast local scratch storage. Absent dedicated GPU acceleration, the resource distribution makes m8idn.large well targeted for web server deployments, API gateways, local caching nodes, microservices, and development database engines requiring responsive NVMe read-write access.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idn.large is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro system. Powered by an Intel processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, the instance delivers 2 vCPUs distributed across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, alongside 8.0 GB of system memory. It features integrated high-speed local storage consisting of a 118 GB NVMe SSD volume, eliminating the overhead of remote block storage for temporary data operations. Networking capability includes a 3 Gbps baseline bandwidth configuration. With a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance balances computational throughput and memory footprint efficiently. Lacking a discrete GPU, m8idn.large focuses its resources on standard application hosting, small caching layers, microservices, local database testing, and general web serving workloads that benefit from high-clock execution and local NVMe scratch space.
